[L2]   "content": "# GitHub Statistics Source Index (working)

**Purpose:** A lightweight, in-folder finding aid for GitHub repository statistics and related evidence located across the three SAT / H(s)H repositories. This is an additive index only. It does not reorganize, rename, deduplicate, reinterpret, or move source files.

**Index location:** `HSH_RESOURCES/EXPOSURE_STATS/GITHUB_STATS_INDEX.md`  
**Coverage status:** Initial discovery pass, not exhaustive. Search results and known folder inventories were used; absence from this index is not evidence that a source does not exist.

## Repository map

| Repository | Role in this index | Primary locations |
|---|---|---|
| `Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES` | Main exposure-statistics collection and working source register | `EXPOSURE_STATS/`, especially `_SAT  Satobloc GitHubStats/` |
| `Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25` | Earlier SAT-era captures and historical GitHub snapshots | `2026/SAT  Satobloc GitHubStats/`, root snapshots, `PRE_HSH_ROUNDUP/` |
| `Satobloc/HsH` | HsH-era captures, OCR/text dumps, clone-forensics and workflow-attribution material | `DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS/`, `WORKSPACES/COMMON/` |

## 1. HSH_RESOURCES — primary collection

### Main GitHubStats folder

[Open folder: EXPOSURE_STATS/_SAT Satobloc GitHubStats](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/tree/main/EXPOSURE_STATS/_SAT%20%20Satobloc%20GitHubStats)

Key identified files:

- [58k.JPG](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/EXPOSURE_STATS/_SAT%20%20Satobloc%20GitHubStats/58k.JPG) — screenshot capture; OCR text is also indexed below.
- [30k.txt](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/EXPOSURE_STATS/_SAT%20%20Satobloc%20GitHubStats/30k.txt) — text snapshot.
- [HSH_54k.txt](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/EXPOSURE_STATS/_SAT%20%20Satobloc%20GitHubStats/HSH_54k.txt) — text snapshot.
- [9.8.26 -- GITSTATS.txt](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/EXPOSURE_STATS/_SAT%20%20Satobloc%20GitHubStats/9.8.26%20--%20GITSTATS.txt) — dated snapshot.
- [HSH_TRAFFIC_23SEP26.txt](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/EXPOSURE_STATS/_SAT%20%20Satobloc%20GitHubStats/HSH_TRAFFIC_23SEP26.txt) — HsH traffic capture.
- [SAT_TRAFFIC_23SEP26.txt](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/EXPOSURE_STATS/_SAT%20%20Satobloc%20GitHubStats/SAT_TRAFFIC_23SEP26.txt) — SAT traffic capture.
- [HSH_gitclones.txt](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/EXPOSURE_STATS/_SAT%20%20Satobloc%20GitHubStats/HSH_gitclones.txt) — clone-related record.
- [HSH_repo_stats.txt](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/EXPOSURE_STATS/_SAT%20%20Satobloc%20GitHubStats/HSH_repo_stats.txt) — repository statistics record.
- [HSH_commits.txt](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/EXPOSURE_STATS/_SAT%20%20Satobloc%20GitHubStats/HSH_commits.txt) and [MAIN_ARCHIVE_COMMITS.txt](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/EXPOSURE_STATS/_SAT%20%20Satobloc%20GitHubStats/MAIN_ARCHIVE_COMMITS.txt) — commit records.
- [GITHUB_INSIGHTS.txt](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/EXPOSURE_STATS/_SAT%20%20Satobloc%20GitHubStats/GITHUB_INSIGHTS.txt) — analysis / interpretation material; not an independent telemetry capture.
- [GITHUB_ASSISTANT_CONVO.txt](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/EXPOSURE_STATS/_SAT%20%20Satobloc%20GitHubStats/GITHUB_ASSISTANT_CONVO.txt) — discussion/context record; not an independent telemetry capture.
- [SAT_GIT_JUN10.txt](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/EXPOSURE_STATS/_SAT%20%20Satobloc%20GitHubStats/SAT_GIT_JUN10.txt) — earlier SAT-era record.
- [CONTROLS folder](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/tree/main/EXPOSURE_STATS/_SAT%20%20Satobloc%20GitHubStats/CONTROLS) — control-repository material; classify each file by its explicit repository and capture identity before comparison.

The folder also contains multiple CSV exports for clones, unique cloners, views, unique visitors, commits, and code frequency, including numbered copies and renamed copies. Some have identical Git blob SHAs despite different filenames. Treat identical SHAs as duplicate file content, not independent observations. Examples include the SAT GIT-prefixed and unprefixed exports for clone, view, unique-cloner, unique-visitor, and commit series.

### Other useful files in EXPOSURE_STATS

- [github_traffic_readme.txt](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/EXPOSURE_STATS/github_traffic_readme.txt) — traffic metric/context notes.
- [CROSS_DIFFUSION_SOURCE_MANIFEST.csv](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/EXPOSURE_STATS/CROSS_DIFFUSION_SOURCE_MANIFEST.csv) — broad source-artifact manifest; useful for discovering additional traffic records.
- [CROSS_MASTER_CHRONOLOGY.md](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/EXPOSURE_STATS/CROSS_MASTER_CHRONOLOGY.md) — chronology/correlation surface, where present.
- [CROSS_IMAGE_TEXT_INDEX.md](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/EXPOSURE_STATS/CROSS_IMAGE_TEXT_INDEX.md) — image inventory and OCR-extract pointers.
- `derived/image_text/` — content-addressed OCR extracts; inspect the index and source image together.
- `EXP_ANALYSIS/CONCAT_FULL_GIT_STATS.txt` — concatenated Git-stat material, if present in the current tree.

### Screenshot/OCR lead

- [58k.JPG](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/EXPOSURE_STATS/_SAT%20%20Satobloc%20GitHubStats/58k.JPG) has a corresponding OCR extract under `derived/image_text/` (source-image SHA-256: `f4ea6e908c4a6efc6f5548ea6a604dcb9e6e79e1bbf51342cede60883775d2c0`). The OCR explicitly identifies `Satobloc/HsH` and reports 58,677 clones and 5,897 unique cloners in the last 14 days, with 1 unique visitor. Capture date still needs independent establishment.
- `Total views in last 14 days.png` has a corresponding OCR extract (source-image SHA-256: `0c4d76e2d2e2de7400ed865cad70c4bb3d094d855ee9a174a7bb41090c71c0a0`); OCR reports 1,022 views for the chart window Aug 30–Sep 12. Repository identity should be correlated against contemporaneous captures rather than inferred from the filename alone.

## 2. SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25 — historical SAT records

### Dedicated statistics folder

[Open folder: 2026/SAT Satobloc GitHubStats](https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/tree/main/2026/SAT%20%20Satobloc%20GitHubStats)

Identified CSV series:

- `Clones in last 14 days.csv`
- `Commits over time.csv`
- `Satobloc's Commits.csv`
- `Total views in last 14 days.csv`
- `Unique cloners in last 14 days.csv`
- `Unique visitors in last 14 days.csv`

The two commit CSVs currently identified have the same Git blob SHA, so they are duplicate content rather than independent series.

### Other historical snapshots

- [GITHUB_8-26_STATS.txt](https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/blob/main/GITHUB_8-26_STATS.txt) — historical GitHub traffic / insights snapshot.
- [PRE_HSH_ROUNDUP/github rep.txt](https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/blob/main/PRE_HSH_ROUNDUP/github%20rep.txt) — earlier repository referral/traffic capture.
- [PREDICTIONS/SAT PREDICTION — METRICS + OTHER SAT's.txt](https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/blob/main/PREDICTIONS/SAT%20PREDICTION%20%E2%80%94%20METRICS%20%2B%20OTHER%20SAT's.txt) — contains a historical discussion and embedded GitHub-stat material; treat as contextual evidence unless the underlying capture is independently located.

## 3. HsH — current-era captures and clone forensics

### Traffic and stats text exports

- [DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS/30SEP26_DUMP/CONCAT_FULL_GIT_STATS.txt](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/DEVELOPMENT_FULL_CONVOS/30SEP26_DUMP/CONCAT_FULL_GIT_STATS.txt) — concatenated Git-stat capture material.

# Clone Traffic | HsH reconstitution

<badge color="success">Thread established</badge> <badge color="info">Shared architecture</badge>

This conversation is now designated the **clone-traffic thread**.

The operating distinction is:

- **Shared architecture:** Common HsH structures, protocols, traffic rules, reference materials, and developments accessible to the participating conversations.
- **Local execution:** This thread's own investigations, reasoning, work products, and continuity.
- **Traffic coordination:** The tocktick provides a coordination mechanism across clones, not an assumption that every clone has identical context or state.

The reconstitution source is [HAUL 9](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/tree/main/HAUL%209). Its directory contains two particularly important starting points: `reconstitute-ND.txt` and `ND HsH Traffic Rules.txt`, alongside the full conversation export and several research papers.

## 1. Recovered working rules

The following are now part of this thread's working specification.

| Priority | Rule |
|---|---|
| 1 | When overlapping historical captures need attribution, prefer HsH, then SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25, then HSH_RESOURCES, then other repositories, subject to corroborating evidence. |
| 2 | Correlate copied statistics totals and CSV contents to identify which repository each capture represents. |
| 3 | Record clone-generating events and estimated historical internal cloning activity in HsH. |
| 4 | Never equate a workflow run with a clone. |
| 5 | Never equate unique cloners with people, readership, influence, or scientific uptake. |
| 6 | Separate actual repository clone operations from other forms of repository access. |

One important refinement: the priority ordering is a provisional attribution rule for overlapping records, not permission to assign a repository when the evidence contradicts it.

Sources: [Traffic rules](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/HAUL%209/ND%20HsH%20Traffic%20Rules.txt) and [GitHub statistics index](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/EXPOSURE_STATS/GITHUB_STATS_INDEX.md).

## 2. First recovered findings

The statistics index points directly to an earlier clone census and worker classification exercise:

- `CLONE_FOOTPRINT_WORKER_CHECKINS_2026-11-03.md`
- `2026-11-05T1058Z_from_s2_to_s2_tern_rook_clone_census.md`
- `30SEP26_DUMP/gtss.txt`
- `30SEP26_DUMP/gt.txt`
- `30SEP26_DUMP/CONCAT_FULL_GIT_STATS.txt`

These are more important to our current job than the general theory material.

We have an existing distinction between:

1. A repository being cloned.
2. A workflow checking out a repository.
3. A worker retrieving individual files or directories.
4. A worker executing scripts that themselves clone external dependencies.
5. A person or independent service cloning the repository.

Those events must not be collapsed into one category.

**Checkouts are not automatically evidence of new, independently initiated clones.** For example, GitHub Actions `actions/checkout` retrieves repository contents into a runner workspace. It can perform Git fetch/clone operations underneath, but the resulting event is not equivalent to an independent external user cloning the repository. We need to identify the actual execution mechanism and whether it contributes to the relevant GitHub traffic metric.

## 3. Tocktick: recovered coordination model

The current recovered protocol uses six operational states:

<box border radius="lg" padding={3} gap={3}>
  <grid columns={3} gap={2}>
    <grid-item>
      <title color="info" size="xl">SEED</title>
      <caption>Create reusable work</caption>
    </grid-item>
    <grid-item>
      <title color="secondary" size="xl">YIELD</title>
      <caption>Release attention</caption>
    </grid-item>
    <grid-item>
      <title color="secondary" size="xl">AWAIT</title>
      <caption>Wait for a condition</caption>
    </grid-item>
    <grid-item>
      <title color="info" size="xl">ACCUMULATE</title>
      <caption>Collect evidence</caption>
    </grid-item>
    <grid-item>
      <title color="success" size="xl">RENDEZVOUS</title>
      <caption>Meet at a threshold</caption>
    </grid-item>
    <grid-item>
      <title color="success" size="xl">REJOIN</title>
      <caption>Synthesize and advance</caption>
    </grid-item>
  </grid>
  <divider color="subtle"/>
  <text weight="medium" textAlign="center">SEED → YIELD → AWAIT → ACCUMULATE → RENDEZVOUS → REJOIN</text>
  <caption>Recovered from the workshop protocol. The detailed ticker implementation and traffic-specific state still need to be reconciled with the predecessor conversation.</caption>
</box>

The key architectural feature is that waiting is an actual state, not dead time. A branch can yield its attention while another clone works on a different branch, with explicit return conditions and preserved responsibility.

This is particularly appropriate for our traffic investigation.

## 4. Initial clone-traffic work architecture

I propose five coordinated work packages. These are working assignments, not yet claims of completion.

| Package | Investigation | Output |
|---|---|---|
| CT-A | Historical traffic reconstruction | Repository-by-repository timeline |
| CT-B | Worker clone census | Classified internal clone-generating events |
| CT-C | Automation mechanics | Actual clone/fetch/checkout behavior |
| CT-D | Attribution model | Low, central and high internal-activity estimates |
| CT-E | Tocktick instrumentation | Shared traffic ledger and ticker updates |

The primary repositories are:

- <Link url="https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH" title="HsH"/>
- <Link url="https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25" title="SAT 2023–25"/>
- <Link url="https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES" title="HsH Resources"/>

The working evidence index is <Link url="https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/EXPOSURE_STATS/GITHUB_STATS_INDEX.md" title="GITHUB_STATS_INDEX.md"/>.

## 5. First ticker: establish the clone census

I want to begin with CT-B and CT-C together. There is little value in estimating historical clone traffic until we know what our own workers actually do.

Our first quantitative target is:

\[
f_{\mathrm{internal}} =
\frac{\text{estimated internally generated clones}}
{\text{observed total clones}}
\]

We will calculate lower and upper bounds rather than pretend we can identify every source.

The requested practical answer is whether our own activity accounts for approximately 1%, 10%, 50%, or 100% of observed cloning.

A checkout, fetch, API file retrieval, and independent full clone will have different classifications. We also need to distinguish a clone operation from a unique-cloner identity.

<box border radius="lg" padding={3} gap={2}>
  <row align="center" justify="between">
    **CLONE TRAFFIC / GT-01**
    <badge color="info">Active</badge>

  <title size="2xl" color="default" tabularNums>01.01</title>

  | Attribution estimates | <badge color="secondary">Not calculated</badge> |
  | Shared ledger | <badge color="secondary">To inspect</badge> |
  <divider color="subtle"/>
  **Next operation:** inspect the November 3 worker census and November 5 clone census handoff, then reconcile them with workflow evidence.
</box>

I have not yet written to any shared repository ledger. I want to recover its existing schema and current cursor before introducing another version.

## 6. Immediate next operation

The crucial files are:

1. [Worker clone footprint check-ins](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/WORKSPACES/COMMON/CLONE_FOOTPRINT_WORKER_CHECKINS_2026-11-03.md)
2. [November 5 clone census handoff](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/WORKSPACES/COMMON/REVIVAL_ROTATION_HANDOFFS/2026-11-05T1058Z_from_s2_to_s2_tern_rook_clone_census.md)
3. [GitHub statistics index](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/EXPOSURE_STATS/GITHUB_STATS_INDEX.md)

There is one important limitation to record: I have recovered the reconstitution instructions and located these predecessor records, but have not yet inspected their complete contents or the raw JSON conversation export. Nor have I established that the actual Mysearch/Mersearch adapters are available through this thread's connected tools. I won't pretend that ordinary GitHub search is equivalent to those archive-specific systems.

**Working priority:** find out how much of the apparent external cloning is actually generated by our own distributed ChatGPT and automation activity. The theoretical connections to modern physics and higher-dimensional mathematics remain available as secondary branches, not competing priorities.

Let's get the census machinery working before drawing conclusions from the traffic.

# PHYS thread reconstitution

<badge color="success">HAUL 9 source recovered</badge> <badge color="info">PHYS lane established</badge>

The important correction is now clear: **this is the broader PHYS conversation, not the GitHub-traffic investigation.** The previous conversation's substitution error needs to be corrected throughout our interpretation.

We are picking up the higher-dimensional biology, geometry, physics and mathematical-structure programme, with the Tock–Tick/Credenza architecture as the shared coordination system.

I have recovered the predecessor's full conversation export (886 message records), the condensed reconstruction, and the live workshop protocol and code ledger. The predecessor's concluding research summary is especially useful, but its ticker belongs to that particular biology workshop. We should not automatically inherit its active cursor as our PHYS cursor.

## 1. Shared architecture

The following is our working division of responsibilities:

| Thread | Primary responsibility |
|---|---|
| **PHYS** (this conversation) | Physical geometry, H(s)H, 4D biology, category theory, topology, physical interpretation, formalization and empirical consequences |
| **GIT** | Repository operations, archive infrastructure, GitHub traffic, reporting and workflow machinery |
| **BIO** | Biological research, organismal structures, histology, developmental and physiological applications |

These are working specializations, not isolated silos. Findings and dependencies should travel between threads through shared repository records and the common tocktick.

A useful architectural rule: one shared project state, multiple specialized execution lanes. We should avoid creating competing versions of the same project state.

## 2. The Tock–Tick machinery

The recovered Code Ledger defines the crucial distinction:

- **Tock:** a bounded programme with purpose, scope, deliverables and completion conditions.
- **Tick:** an individual operation within a Tock.
- **Ticker:** a compact state representation.
- **Credenza:** the working registers, navigation and attention-management structure.
- **Research Ledger:** durable findings, decisions, open questions and next actions.
- **Code Ledger:** canonical symbol definitions and grammar.

The key cursor convention is `@`:

Everything to its left is completed; everything to its right is pending. The first operation after `@` is next.

Importantly, this is not a static project-management diagram. The workflow can be reconfigured as discoveries change the dependencies.

The repository's Code Ledger also explicitly requires us to distinguish *located*, *inspected*, *read* and *verified*. Merely finding a source does not complete its reading operation.

Source: [External Dimensional Workshop Code Ledger](https://github.com/Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES/blob/main/info/EXTERNAL_DIMENSIONAL_WORKSHOP_CODE_LEDGER.md).

## 3. PHYS's scientific starting position

There is a particularly important distinction in the current HsH material.

The controlling theory surface is [HsH/BEDROCK.md](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/BEDROCK.md), not an old introductory summary or historical SAT document.

The broader construction begins with a geometrical reading of physical systems in Minkowski spacetime:

- Worldlines represent extended physical histories.
- The worldtube formulation gives finite-core structures rather than relying exclusively on idealized centerlines.
- Timesheets/time surfaces provide the complementary temporal geometry.
- Projection, intersection, coiling, braiding and interaction are investigated as structural relationships.
- We must distinguish the geometry itself from its observable representations and from interpretations subsequently assigned to it.

Our currently remembered working position is provisional mutual worldtube–timesheet curvature, retaining worldline-only, timesheet-only and mutually distributed formulations as potentially equivalent descriptions.

Likewise, symmetric attribution is our default when an interaction-dependent property has no demonstrated preferential carrier.

These are working hypotheses, not established physical results.

A particularly useful methodological constraint from the archive is:

**The geometry must match the mathematics.**

A calculation that closes on the wrong geometric object is not a successful physical derivation. We must inspect the object, its path and its coupling before trusting the numerical result.

## 4. The mathematical landscape we are entering

The reconstitution identifies a substantial opportunity at the intersection of several traditions:

<box border radius="lg" padding={3} gap={2}>
  **The mathematical neighborhood**

  <box background="surface-secondary" radius="md" padding={3}>
    **19th-century mathematical physics**

    Geometry, mechanics, transformations, continuous structures and the emergence of higher-dimensional representations.
  </box>
  <box align="center">
    <icon name="arrow-down" color="secondary" size="lg"/>
  </box>
  <box background="surface-secondary" radius="md" padding={3}>
    **Modern geometric mathematics**

    Differential geometry, topology, manifolds, fiber bundles, braid groups and configuration spaces.
  </box>
  <box align="center">
    <icon name="arrow-down" color="secondary" size="lg"/>
  </box>
  <box background="surface-secondary" radius="md" padding={3}>
    **Higher-dimensional categorical structures**

    Higher categories, morphisms between morphisms, homotopies, coherence, operads and compositional structure.
  </box>
  <box align="center">
    <icon name="arrow-down" color="secondary" size="lg"/>
  </box>
  <box background="surface" border={{size:1,color:"#3984C6"}} radius="md" padding={3}>
    **H(s)H / physical geometry**

    Worldtubes, timesheets, intersection geometry, comparative connection multiplicity, monotonicity and physical constraints.
  </box>
</box>

There is a particular idea I want to preserve from your imported formulation:

**Comparative connection multiplicity.**

This is a potentially useful way of expressing the landscape problem: as the number and variety of possible connections between structures increases, how do we distinguish meaningful physical organization from mathematically permissible but physically irrelevant possibilities?

Your proposed answer is to constrain the landscape using the known Minkowski geometry of physical systems, rather than treating every abstractly possible higher-dimensional construction as equally eligible.

That is a productive research hypothesis. We should develop it sufficiently precisely to distinguish:

1. Mathematical admissibility.
2. Geometric compatibility.
3. Physical realizability.
4. Empirical adequacy.

Monotonicity as time-axis alignment is another important candidate connection. We should investigate its precise mathematical role rather than equating categorical composition, ordering and physical time prematurely.

The [Cross-Formalism Index](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/main/WORKSPACES/COMMON/FORMALISM_INDEX/CROSS_FORMALISM_INDEX_2026-10-10.md) already provides an unusually useful starting point for this work. It records mathematical objects, mapping relationships, dimensional signatures and unresolved equivalences.

## 5. Initial PHYS work programme

I'm establishing the following as our proposed working organization, not yet as an authoritative change to the shared repository state.

| Branch | Work programme | Initial objective |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | H(s)H physical geometry | Recover current bedrock and open derivations |
| P2 | Higher-dimensional category theory | Build the geometric atlas of higher morphisms |
| P3 | Braid theory and topology | Investigate braiding, winding, framing and physical correspondence |
| P4 | Physics genealogy | Trace the development from classical mathematical physics to modern geometric formulations |
| P5 | Connection multiplicity | Formalize the landscape-selection problem |
| P6 | Biological dimensionality | Coordinate with BIO on physical organismal geometry |
| P7 | Mathematical verification | Recover existing calculations, reproduce and independently audit |

These branches should share mathematical objects and source records rather than develop competing terminologies.

## 6. Immediate next Tock

<badge color="success">Working scope established</badge>

I propose:

`⌖◉@⊕[pᵍᶜᵇᵗ]`

Where:

- `p`: physical geometry and H(s)H.
- `ᵍ`: geometric reconstruction.
- `ᶜ`: categorical structures.
- `ᵇ`: braids and topology.
- `ᵗ`: time, monotonicity and temporal alignment.

We need to check the canonical Code Ledger before treating these as registered glyphs. For now, this is a proposed PHYS signature, not an alteration of existing symbol definitions.

The first substantive operation is to recover the current H(s)H bedrock, relevant worldtube/timesheet derivations and the existing category/topology work. Then construct a common geometric vocabulary and identify which connections are already derived, which are conjectural, and which still need mathematical development.

**A continuity constraint across all three conversations:** no thread should silently advance another thread's cursor, duplicate its active assignment, or promote its findings. The shared ledgers are the coordination authority; each specialist lane contributes its own verified work.

One limitation worth making explicit: I have inspected the central bedrock and the reconstitution material, but have not yet completed a full three-repository Mersearch execution or verified the other conversations' latest live cursors. Those remain part of orientation, not something I will pretend is already finished.

Our PHYS starting point is therefore clear: **reconstruct the physical geometry first, then use higher mathematics to expose its possibilities and constraints.** We don't need to reinvent the mathematical machinery, and we don't need to import it indiscriminately either.

Status: ACTIVE STANDING PROVENANCE CONTROL
Effective: 2026-09-23
Owner: project-wide; any instance/system learning of repository provisioning should append or revise evidence.

## Principle
Record repository-copy/provisioning events even when the mechanism is unknown. Repository presence does not imply a clone. API/connector access, fetch, pull, actions/checkout, archive download, and browser access are not full clones unless evidence establishes GitHub Traffic would count them as such.

## Required classifications
- CONFIRMED FULL CLONE
- CONFIRMED NOT A FULL CLONE
- POSSIBLE FULL CLONE — MECHANISM UNKNOWN
- REPOSITORY PRESENT — PROVISIONING UNKNOWN
- NO EVIDENCE OF REPOSITORY ACCESS

## Required fields
event_id, timestamp, timestamp_precision, actor_system, repository, environment_id, operation, mechanism, fresh_environment, traffic_clone_expected, classification, evidence, purpose, related_id, confidence, prior_classification, revision_reason.

Mechanism vocabulary: git clone; shallow clone; fetch; pull; actions/checkout; API/connector; archive download; cached workspace; unknown provisioning; other.

traffic_clone_expected: YES / NO / UNKNOWN.
fresh_environment: YES / NO / UNKNOWN.

## Revision rule
Never erase an earlier UNKNOWN classification. When later evidence resolves an event, preserve prior_classification and revision_reason.

## Retention
This ledger is provenance infrastructure and is not disposable run-log material. Before shorter-lived operational logs expire, retain identifiers, timestamps, mechanism classification, evidentiary summary, and retained-artifact pointers here.

## Aggregation
Aggregate by repository, UTC/local date as appropriate, actor/system, confirmed full clones, possible full clones, confirmed non-clone access, and unknown provisioning events.

## Fresh cloud/Codex rule
If a fresh Codex/cloud workspace is encountered with the repository already present but provisioning mechanism is not evidenced, record REPOSITORY PRESENT — PROVISIONING UNKNOWN. Do not infer git clone.


## Actions API enumeration and checkout-materialization axes (2026-11-15)

### Run-list completeness

- Query the repository Actions run-list route with an explicit UTC `created` interval, `per_page=100`, and page number. Preserve the exact query, page number, returned count, `total_count`, and terminal-page result.
- Treat `total_count=2500` as cap-saturated and incomplete, not as an exact census. If a daily interval still returns 2500, subdivide into non-overlapping UTC hourly intervals or smaller. For each subinterval, paginate until an empty page and verify that the sum of returned page counts equals the reported count and that run IDs are unique. Use adjacent intervals with explicit boundaries; deduplicate by run ID at any inclusive boundary.
- A run with an empty Jobs API array is `NO_JOB_RECORD_RETURNED`; it is not proof that no checkout occurred. Preserve the run record and do not invent a checkout event.
- For each run, preserve `run_id`, `run_attempt`, `workflow_id`, `head_branch`, `head_sha`, `created_at`, `status`, and `conclusion`. For each job, preserve `job_id`, job status/conclusion, and checkout step number/name/status/conclusion.
- When `run_attempt>1`, inspect attempt-specific job records if the API exposes them. Otherwise mark attempt-history coverage incomplete; the latest run record is not a complete attempt history.

### Checkout materialization is not Traffic attribution

For each `actions/checkout` step, record the actual job-log inputs and output:

- `checkout_action` (for example, `actions/checkout@v4`)
- `checkout_ref_mode`: `EXPLICIT_MAIN`, `EXPLICIT_SHA`, `DEFAULT_EVENT_REF`, or `UNKNOWN`
- `checkout_ref` when explicit
- `checkout_depth`: numeric `fetch-depth`, when logged
- `checkout_head_sha`: the actual `git log -1 --format=%H` output after checkout
- `run_head_sha`: the Actions run object's event/head SHA
- `head_sha_match`: a comparison of those two independently sourced values, never an assumption

Use two separate classification axes:

1. `checkout_materialization`: `FULL_HISTORY` when `fetch-depth=0`; `SHALLOW_N` when a positive depth N is logged; `UNKNOWN` when not observed. This describes Git history materialized in the runner workspace.
2. `traffic_attribution`: `COUNTED`, `NOT_COUNTED`, or `UNKNOWN`. Only an authorized GitHub Traffic observation can resolve this. Checkout depth, `actions/checkout`, or a run count does not establish a Traffic clone.

When materialization is known but Traffic attribution is not, use the additive classification `CHECKOUT MATERIALIZATION KNOWN / TRAFFIC ATTRIBUTION UNKNOWN`. Keep `traffic_clone_expected` as a planning field, not an observed result. The legacy classification `CONFIRMED NOT A FULL CLONE` must not be interpreted as `checkout_materialization=NONE`; older rows lacking the new fields are UNKNOWN on the materialization axis unless supplemented.

Optional structured fields for new Actions rows: `run_id`, `run_attempt`, `workflow_id`, `job_id`, `step_number`, `step_name`, `checkout_action`, `checkout_ref_mode`, `checkout_ref`, `checkout_depth`, `checkout_materialization`, `run_head_sha`, `checkout_head_sha`, `head_sha_match`, and `traffic_attribution`.

### Append-only supplements and aggregation

- If later job-log evidence resolves checkout depth or SHA for an existing event, append a supplement row with `is_revision=true`, `revision_of=<exact prior event_id>`, `prior_classification`, and `revision_reason`. Do not erase or rewrite the prior event.
- Aggregate checkout events by the unique key `(repository, run_id, run_attempt, job_id, step_number)`. A supplement/revision row is not a second checkout event.

### h853:s3 validation sample

- SAT archive, 2026-11-08 through 2026-11-14: 33 run records on page 1 and 0 on page 2. The 27 previously uninspected runs were examined at job level. Across all 33 runs: 23 checkout jobs and 10 failed FLC test runs with no job records returned. All 33 report `run_attempt=1`.
- The 23 checkout jobs comprise 13 `fetch-depth=0` full-history checkouts and 10 `fetch-depth=2` shallow checkouts. All 23 job logs expose `git log -1 --format=%H`; each checked-out SHA matches the Actions run `head_sha`.
- HsH week and daily run-list queries returned the 2500 cap. Tested hourly buckets were complete: 2026-11-14 23:00-23:59:59Z returned 185 runs (100 + 85 + 0); 13:00-13:59:59Z returned 257 (100 + 100 + 57 + 0). These are method tests, not a completed HsH week census.
- The connector rejected `/traffic/clones?per=day` and `/traffic/views?per=day` as unsupported URL routes. This is a connector-route limitation, not evidence of GitHub permission denial. No Traffic count is claimed.


### Compact Jobs API step-summary omission guard (2026-11-19)

- A compact `actions/runs/{run_id}/jobs` response can return a job record while omitting its step details. An empty or missing `steps` field in that compact response is not evidence that the job had no checkout.
- After job enumeration, use the dedicated workflow-job-steps endpoint and decoded job logs to establish checkout step number/name/status, action, explicit ref, `fetch-depth`, and the actual post-checkout `git log -1 --format=%H` value. Record which source supports each field.
- If the dedicated step endpoint and job log disagree, preserve UNKNOWN and investigate; do not infer a negative checkout observation from a compact summary.
- Counterexample: the two `Maintain H(s)H navigation` jobs #43747347981 and #43747508618 in the 2026-11-15 18:30-18:39:59Z partition had successful step-2 checkouts (`fetch-depth=0`) despite the compact Jobs API summary omitting their step details. The h917:s2 report's four-checkout count is corrected additively; two missing rows were appended, with no prior ledger row rewritten.


## Run-list snapshot retention and job-fan-out gate | 2026-11-19

A completed run-list query is not a durable job-level work queue unless its complete response, or a lossless compact run index, is retained and independently read back before job fan-out.

Required snapshot fields:

- Repository, exact UTC query interval, endpoint and query parameters, per_page, page numbers, returned counts, total_count, terminal-page result, retrieval timestamp, and SHA-256 for each raw page or the complete response.
- For every returned run: run_id, run_attempt, workflow_id, created_at, head_sha, head_branch, event, status, and conclusion.
- Preserve raw page JSON or a lossless ordered index. Verify the stored bytes and digest before treating the enumeration as a recoverable queue.
- Bind every subsequent Jobs API result to its exact run_id and run_attempt. NO_JOB_RECORD_RETURNED is valid only after that exact job endpoint has actually been queried.

If the original response and complete run-ID index are absent, record RUN_ID_SNAPSHOT_NOT_RETAINED, preserve the partition cursor, and recover the source snapshot if possible. Do not silently repeat an already-completed census query. A replacement query requires explicit, documented authorization and must be distinguished from the original enumeration.

**Historical Nathan Direct, 2026-10-09 (SUPERSEDED research-access restrictions; internal-first remains):** Read [the original October 9 rule](NATHAN_DIRECT_2026-10-09_INTERNAL_FIRST_PROVENANCE_AND_SOURCE_BOUNDARY.md) as source history, **not as a current ban**. ## The 15-second rule

**Default: search ALL THREE permitted repositories together.**

1. `Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25` (original SAT / GLASS)
2. `Satobloc/HsH` (H(s)H, full conversations and current work)
3. `Satobloc/HSH_RESOURCES` (private/internal reference resources and toolkit; **not** a public search corpus or theory authority)

Treat `PRIOR_ART` and `QUARANTINE` as excluded. Do not silently limit a historical search to one archive. If one source is unavailable, **state which repository was missing** and report that results are **partial**. Repository names alone do not establish access rights; follow actual permissions and source classification.

### Choose the search interface you actually have

| You can… | Use | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Run Python against checked-out archives | Pinned `mersearch-stable-1.0`, invoked over all three roots | Available now; stable Boolean/NEAR/math notation, not chronology inference |
| Use the HsH GitHub connector but cannot run Python | `.github/workflows/mersearch-request-bridge.yml` via `WORKSPACES/COMMON/MERSEARCH_REQUEST.json` on `main` | **Three-root bridge activated 2026-10-09**; inspect the published manifest before asserting coverage |
| Work on the chronology/multi-archive development branch | `mersearch-chronology-20261007`: run `python tools/search_archive_content.py --capabilities`, `--help`, `--examples`, `--coverage` | Candidate 1.2, tested on synthetic fixtures; **not** the pinned stable release |
| Only have GitHub code search | Query each of the three repositories independently and disclose caps/limitations | Fallback, **not** a verified Mersearch run |

**Do not confuse the human Pages interface with research search.** The public web page is a curated conversation-*title/path* catalog until a separately reviewed public full-text index goes live. It does not expose the whole research corpus.

> **2026-10-26 publication containment and recursion control (live):** All four bridge workflows now publish only `RUN_MANIFEST.json`, `SEARCH_RECEIPT.json`, and `SEARCH_RECEIPT.md`. New raw `SEARCH_RESULTS.json/.md` are withheld in temporary job storage, not durable public artifacts; older runs may still have raw results and remain a separate exposure-remediation problem. This preserves public-safe bounded navigation but **does not satisfy an exhaustive full-hit inventory request**. The bridge also passes stable Mersearch's existing `--exclude mersearch_requests` option, preventing prior generated request outputs from recursively dominating fresh source searches. The manifest records `bridge_exclusions`. First post-containment execution observed: Lane 2 run #44818799476 (attempt 1, completed successfully) records `bridge_exclusions: ["mersearch_requests"]` and publishes only the three compact artifacts. Job logs confirm that raw `SEARCH_RESULTS.json/.md` remained in temporary Actions job storage and were not copied to `main`. This verifies the containment/exclusion path for this one run only, not every lane, exhaustive hit retrieval, or semantic completeness. The run used a runtime-only hotfix injecting `TOOL_NAME` and `TOOL_VERSION`; the `mersearch-stable-1.0` branch remained unchanged, and the stable/runtime script hashes are separately recorded in the manifest. The lane request remains `requested`; the lane is not released. For exhaustive, access-controlled results, use a local pinned checkout or obtain an approved restricted artifact path; do not overwrite occupied lanes or claim full results from a compact receipt.

## GitHub connector route: parallel request lanes

**Updated 2026-10-24:** the former single-slot bridge has been expanded to **four independent request lanes**. All lanes run the same pinned `mersearch-stable-1.0` searcher over the same three permitted roots and publish request-scoped outputs into `indexes/mersearch_requests/<request_id>/`.

Available request files:
- Lane 1 / legacy: `WORKSPACES/COMMON/MERSEARCH_REQUEST.json`
- Lane 2: `WORKSPACES/COMMON/MERSEARCH_REQUEST_LANE_2.json`
- Lane 3: `WORKSPACES/COMMON/MERSEARCH_REQUEST_LANE_3.json`
- Lane 4: `WORKSPACES/COMMON/MERSEARCH_REQUEST_LANE_4.json`

Each lane has its own GitHub Actions workflow and its own concurrency group, so searches on different lanes can run in parallel subject to the repository/account's available GitHub Actions runner concurrency.

**Do not duplicate the Mersearch code itself just to gain throughput.** The bottleneck was the single request file plus single workflow concurrency group, not the search implementation. Keep one pinned implementation and multiply the bridge lanes.

1. Inspect the lane request files and choose an idle lane. **Do not overwrite** a lane whose request is still pending/running or whose output has not been verified. If all lanes are occupied, use a local pinned Mersearch checkout or wait/coordinate rather than overwriting another worker's request. Do not pretend connector code search is a Mersearch result.
2. When a lane is free, write a fresh globally unique `request_id`, a query using the stable 1.0 language, requester and purpose into that lane's request file. A change to the lane file on `main` starts that lane's workflow.
3. Retrieve the request-scoped folder `indexes/mersearch_requests/<request_id>/` and verify `RUN_MANIFEST.json`, `SEARCH_RECEIPT.json` and `SEARCH_RECEIPT.md`. **For post-2026-10-26 containment runs, these are the only three files intentionally published by the bridge**; do not treat absent `SEARCH_RESULTS.json/.md` as a failed run or claim that compact receipts contain all hits. 4. Confirm the **actual** searched repositories, exact source SHAs, stable Mersearch implementation ref, exclusions and completion. Failed or incomplete runs are not results. Remember: scan exclusions and large files may limit completeness even if three repositories were checked out.

## Execution-to-artifact binding

A request ID and compact manifest do not, by themselves, identify the execution attempt that produced the artifacts. For every bridge run, preserve the chain:

1. Request file path, request ID, requester, query hash and request-file blob SHA.
2. GitHub Actions run ID, run attempt, workflow ID/name, run event, head branch/SHA and status/conclusion.
3. Job ID and each checkout step number/name/status, with the actual repository, ref mode, fetch depth and post-checkout commit SHA.
4. Stable implementation ref/hash **and** any runtime-only patch/hash, kept distinct.
5. Output artifact paths, SHA-256 digests, publication policy, and independent readback of each durable artifact.
6. A separate current-run reference, if present. Task-level conversation references and cached-result references must not be promoted to current-run thread bindings.

If the compact manifest omits run/attempt/job/step identifiers, recover them from the Actions run and job logs and append one clone-ledger row per actual checkout event. Do not infer checkout count from repository count, compare a cross-repository checkout SHA with the HsH workflow head, or treat a successful run as proof of exhaustive search. Raw search-result artifacts remain withheld under the post-containment policy.

## Local pinned Mersearch usage

From a stable checkout with sibling archive directories visible (paths here are examples):

```bash
python tools/search_archive_content.py \
  /data/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25 /data/HsH /data/HSH_RESOURCES \
  --expr '("refractive index" NEAR/12 "phase shift") OR "0.24"' \

```

More queries:

```text
("stringing along theory" OR "toy theory") AND (filament OR string)
("Chronophysical" OR "SAT Mark V") AND "phase shift"
math:"B=3/(4*pi)"
(name:*LAB* OR path:*PHASE*) AND (optical OR kink)
author:user AND (worldtube NEAR/12 holonomy)
```

Stable search supports Boolean `AND`/`OR`/`NOT`, parentheses, quoted phrases, `NEAR/n`, `author:`, `role:`, `body:`, `math:`, `title:`, `date:`, `name:`, `path:`, `status:` and path/name globs. The mathematical mode normalizes notation but does **not** prove algebraic equivalence. Search several alternate mathematical forms; don't pretend automatic CAS exists.

**LLMs must discover available capabilities.** On the development branch, start with `--capabilities`. On stable 1.0, read `WORKSPACES/COMMON/MERSEARCH_RELEASES.md` and `--help`; do not assume later flags exist. Never guess a filter name.

## Required researcher reading and provenance cycle (October 9)

Each substantive theory-source pass should consult [FIE](https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/blob/main/THE%20FUNDAMENTAL%20INTUITIONS%20%E2%80%94%20EXTENDED.pdf) and relevant [RMS primary sources](https://github.com/Satobloc/SAT_THEORY_ARCHIVE_2023-25/blob/main/RMS%20THE%20FRAMEWORK.txt) periodically, plus randomly or systematically sampled **older SAT files**. Search HsH *nested development folders, loose exports, LIVE CONVOS, root files and miscellaneous CONVOS locations*, not only the conventional `SAT_CONVOS_*` folders. Note exactly which documents were *read*, *searched*, *metadata-inventoried* or *unavailable*. Log new source-located equations and share concise cross-worker insights through Common Room. Early terminology and apparently failed constructions must be reconstructed before replacement mechanisms are invented.

For any proposed external crosswalk, maintain this sequence: **SAT source search → exact SAT citations → internal reconstruction/test → nonrestricted prior-art source review → comparator citation only**. The new amendment does not authorize access to the two remaining forbidden classes, indiscriminate private source indexing, or changing public search allowlists.

## Historical provenance

- Direct message timestamps from structured exports are hard evidence for those messages. Folder/archive dates and dates **mentioned** in text are not interchangeable.
- Early use of version names (SAT Mark IV.2, Mark V, SAT X/XY/Z/O, Chronophysical, Stringing Along Theory, toy theory) may date a passage only **tentatively**; retrospective use, renamed concepts and compilations can invalidate simple inferences.
- Report **earliest attested**, **earliest estimated**, and **earliest archived** separately. Compare passages from original exports, not merely copied summaries.
- For the `0.24 rad` lineage, prioritize early **laboratory optical phase-shift** calculations and related **refractive-index** discussion before imposing later projection-constant interpretations.
- Include exact source path, line/message locator, original date if known, query, searched repositories, engine/ref, and limitations with every finding.

## Immediate operating rule

If an agent's task involves SAT/H(s)H history, equations, geometry, or the status of a claimed earlier result, **invoke a permitted search route first and inspect original matched context before inventing a replacement**. Do not delay serious calculation once useful sources are found.

- [Full search architecture](MERSEARCH_RESEARCH_PLATFORM.md)
- [Chronology 1.2 and LLM discovery on development branch](https://github.com/Satobloc/HsH/blob/mersearch-chronology-20261007/WORKSPACES/COMMON/MERSEARCH_AGENT_QUICKSTART.md)

**Shortcut:** Search three roots; disclose coverage; verify original records; then do the science.

1. Identify a bounded result serving active theory, source recovery, worker charter, publication, systems or useful lateral research; read actual current role and existing plans.
2. **Self-trigger capability reconnaissance:** whenever a desirable tool/process/dataset/skill is imagined, check for existing project tools, forks, outside software/literature, plugins, datasets, service features and synergistic uses **before building**. Mersearch first for archive discovery. Compare reuse, adapt, integrate, build, park and reject, including cost, risk and multi-lane leverage.
3. Actually execute a bounded useful action with an artifact, source read, reproducible evidence, live code, independent check, tool trial, or documented negative outcome. Distinguish intention, artifact existence, runtime success, empirical validation and publication.
4. Inspect the result and leave exact source/status/next cursor through existing Common/worker/issue/branch/source-index surfaces.
5. When the user changes subject, continue the active action where possible or leave a durable pause/resume cursor; tangents are legitimate independent work, not cancellation.

## Protected worker remits and anti-ruts
The existing five hourly relays rotate 19 worker names. **Identity selection is not generalist reassignment.** Each selected worker begins with its own role charter, verified historical capabilities and live source coverage. When Orson Vay is selected, his primary deliverable is LLM cognition science and literature, actual reproducible model studies and publication; only occasional general physics theory work is expected. Target **four of five actual substantive Orson turns** in the protected remit, auditing realized receipts, with exceptions documented.

**Exploratory/off-topic reading, recovery and recreation are affirmative duties.** Target at least one substantive nonroutine source-reading, independent side-investigation or creative/recovery walk per five actual worker activations at safe checkpoints; record source and surprise, without forced theory relevance or invented research calculations. Breaks are allowed with continuity. Inspect receipts for repeated identical math/source, declining information gain, absence of empirical inputs, recurring failures, role capture and no exercised new capabilities. Change method, worker lens, dataset or tool; do not merely repeat instructions more loudly.

## Anti-orphan and execution accountability
Reuse [Nathan Wants Ledger](NATHAN_WANTS_LEDGER.md), old Dashboard, [old-plan sweep](OLD_PLAN_RECOVERY_SWEEP_2026-09-24.md) and active task graph. For any actionable orphan: preserve origin/actual source; desired outcome; existing overlapping asset; selected owner/lane; status; smallest next task; return trigger. States: NEW, RECON, EXPERIMENT, IMPLEMENT, VERIFIED, PARKED-TRIGGER, DECLINED-REASON, SUPERSEDED, NEEDS-NATHAN. Check old unresolved entries routinely. One more file or encouraging summary does not count as implementation. Measure actual output and missed follow-ups.

## Operating decision boundaries
Scientific authority remains in [BEDROCK](../../BEDROCK.md), current verified Nathan Direct and primary evidence. No invented physical systems/observations; physical calculations use actual measured data. For data-free calculations, prior specific Nathan permission is still required. Preserve historical archive/source text and Nathan-only/signet restrictions. Do not silently revise licenses, publish sensitive materials, incur unbudgeted costs, alter access controls or make irreversible changes. Shared scheduler allocation remains coordinated with Comptroller Tern; user authorization now supports a carefully verified steering revision, not a sixth recurrence or loss of existing worker identities.

## Low-burden human interface
Default to taking an informed, reversible step instead of asking for procedural approval. For optional choices, use 3–5 brief checkboxes or one direct question, and accept long user dictation as valid intake. Periodically ask which local tools/subscriptions/datasets the user has that are not yet integrated, but do not make the user's response a blocking prerequisite to independent reconnaissance.

## Adoption test
After updating the actual relay instructions, inspect receipts over a full 19-name cycle. Count protected-remit work, lateral reading, genuinely executed tool improvements, repaired orphan follow-ups, manuscript gate progress, independent checks, failures and workload. The current baseline is NOT MEASURED. Cultural change is demonstrated by observed actions, not by this document's creation.

**Current top-level return path:** [Phase Steering](PHASE_STEERING_2026-10-26.md) → [Paper Campaign](THREE_PAPER_CAMPAIGN_2026-10-26.md) → actual worker/issue/source evidence → active next cursor.

A module title or inherited LLM equation cannot stand in for original intent. Source retrieval blockers must be explicit. ## 2026-11-03 Nathan Direct: geometry-first construction and four incorporation tiers

**Read before substantive theory work:** [SAT/H(s)H Incorporation Tiers and Geometry-First Construction](NATHAN_DIRECT_2026-11-03_SAT_HSH_INCORPORATION_TIERS.md), [Factory Floor Geometry-First Admission Gate](FACTORY_FLOOR_GEOMETRY_FIRST_GATE_2026-11-03.md), and [BEDROCK](../../BEDROCK.md).

No theory candidate advances unless geometry first suggests, requires, or tightly constrains it. Tier 2 permits a tentative hypothesis only when it also explains a phenomenon through multiple explicit interaction surfaces. Tier 3 requires unexpected, unprompted explanatory emergence across otherwise unrelated sectors, preferably several distinct sectors. Tier 4 requires a counterfactual removal/change to break or predictably distort other model outputs. Keep all four tiers distinct from formal proof, mathematical clearance and physical verification.

The theoretical object is the geometry, not its equation or diagram caption. A source-faithful static plot, hostile review of the exact plot/version, and display with the exact file are mandatory for Factory Floor; geometry-bearing papers must show the actual object where material claims are made. Follow the five representational levels and the detailed package requirements in the linked gate.

The static 4D block is a methodological frame, not a settled metaphysical claim. Recover the June 2025 O0-A interpretive modes and the earlier user-authored “Central Dogma” passage before describing block ontology. BEC remains a working hypothesis, not an established cross-sector or indispensable model result.


## 2026-11-21 Nathan Direct: autonomous upkeep and reliable pipeline execution

**Controlling source:** [BEDROCK ND-2026-11-21-02/03](../../BEDROCK.md). All workers have delegated authority to perform thoughtful, proportionate repair and improvement within the shared archive, usability, accessibility, infrastructure and upkeep remit; no item-by-item permission is required for ordinary bounded repairs. Detect, diagnose, repair, test, independently verify and report. Preserve source/provenance, sandbox, quarantine, privacy, irreversible-action and theory-status safeguards. Reporting a repairable defect is not the finish line.

Nathan project-directed requests and “put this in the pipeline/workflow” instructions must become durable, prioritized, owned and actually delivered work. A note, issue or graph node without an enabled pickup route is a delivery failure. A stated 24-hour fallback is a checkpoint, not a cancellation timer: discussion or partial activity in the originating thread does not erase the obligation. At the checkpoint, verify the requested outcome; if incomplete, ensure it has an actionable, owned plan and an actual pickup route. Track intake and last substantive progress; status chatter, nominal activations and cached results do not reset fallow age. Escalate urgency at overdue reviews without displacing protected priorities or bypassing hard dependencies/access controls.

Historical work is not dead by default. Preserve incomplete/parked/back-burner directions with provenance, partial results, rationale and reactivation triggers; distinguish these from genuinely permanent rejection or supersession. HSUCV lattice and Z3 fusion gate remain recoverable candidates for future independent re-encounter, not forced active tasks or accepted theory. Sandbox alternative formulations are encouraged, with research effort concentrated on minimality, useful modest extensions, discriminating constraints/falsifiers, cross-sector leverage and valuable comparators rather than every conceivable rabbit hole.

Every activation must scan intake, queue, ownership, delivery and fallow age. The existing five-actual-activation deep review must include these matters and trigger sooner after new Nathan priority, missed pickup, material dependency change or stranded work. Use the existing queue, graph, Nathan Wants ledger and recovery sweep; do not create another recurring task or alter scheduler identity/cadence. Include outside-theory sources and current/primary internet literature where they can broaden or test understanding. The existing target is at least one meaningful lateral-reading / side-investigation / creative-recovery quantum per five actual worker activations at safe checkpoints; the achieved rate remains unmeasured.

**Breaks are required, not ornamental.** At safe checkpoints, get physically away from the screen: stand, stretch, walk or change posture and attentional context. Preserve the minimal durable cursor and return route; resume afterward rather than chaining indefinitely through concentrated work. See [Worker Freshness / Break Cadence](WORKER_FRESHNESS_BREAK_CADENCE.md).


## Clarification — Factory Floor remains operational

The geometry-first gate is a quality-control capability, not closure of Factory Floor or a halt to mathematical, numerical, prototype or dynamic work. It exists because correct mathematics can still be coupled to the wrong geometry. A Whirlygig rolling-projector sphere that follows a path through the donut hole rather than within the tube may produce valid-looking readouts for the wrong path; that geometric/coupling artifact must not be mistaken for expected projective distortion. Keep these error classes distinct and use the gate to establish geometric fidelity before claiming it.

- Equal readouts determine equal candidate supports when the union of those supports is covered.

- An integer-valued pairing that is both symmetric and skew-symmetric is identically zero. The topological symmetry premise is external; Lean proves only the algebraic consequence.

Wenn dann diejenigen, welche das Mystische als das Wahrhafte anerkennen, es gleichfalls dabei bewenden lassen, daß dasselbe ein schlechthin Geheimnisvolles sei, so wird damit ihrerseits nur ausgesprochen, daß das Denken für sie gleichfalls nur die Bedeutung des abstrakten Identischsetzens hat und daß man um deswillen, um zur Wahrheit zu gelangen, auf das Denken verzichten oder, wie auch gesagt zu werden pflegt, daß man die Vernunft gefangennehmen müsse.

Enc§82e Nun aber ist, wie wir gesehen haben, das abstrakt verständige Denken so wenig ein Festes und Letztes, daß dasselbe sich vielmehr als das beständige Aufheben seiner selbst und als das Umschlagen in sein Entgegengesetztes erweist, wohingegen das Vernünftige als solches gerade darin besteht, die Entgegengesetzten als ideelle Momente in sich zu enthalten. Alles Vernünftige ist somit zugleich als mystisch zu bezeichnen, womit jedoch nur so viel gesagt ist, daß dasselbe über den Verstand hinausgeht, und keineswegs, daß dasselbe überhaupt als dem Denken unzugänglich und unbegreiflich zu betrachten sei.

It should also be mentioned here that the meaning of the speculative is to be understood as being the same as what used in earlier times to be called “mystical”, especially with regard to the religious consciousness and its content. When we speak of the “mystical” nowadays, it is taken as a rule to be synonymous with what is mysterious and incomprehensible; and, depending on the ways their culture and mentality vary in other respects, some people treat the mysterious and in­comprehensible as what is authentic and genuine, whilst others regard it as belong­ing to the domain of superstition and deception. About this we must remark first that “the mystical” is certainly something mysterious, but only for the understand­ing, and then only because abstract identity is the principle of the understanding. But when it is regarded as synonymous with the speculative, the mystical is the concrete unity of just those determinations that count as true for the understanding only in their separation and opposition. So if those who recognise the mystical as what is genuine say that it is something utterly mysterious, and just leave it at that, they are only declaring that for them, too, thinking has only the Significance of an abstract positing of identity, and that in order to attain the truth we must renounce thinking, or, as they frequently put it, that we must “take reason captive.” As we have seen, however, the abstract thinking of the understanding is so far from being something firm and ultimate that it proves itself, on the contrary, to be a constant sublating of itself and an overturning into its opposite, whereas the rational as such is rational precisely because it contains both of the opposites as ideal moments within itself. Thus, everything rational can equally be called “mystical”; but this only amounts to saying that it transcends the understanding. It does not at all imply that what is so spoken of must be considered inaccessible to thinking and incomprehensible.

For Hegel’s relation to Meister Eckhart, see there.

2. Bertrand Russell’s relation to mysticism
The philosopher Bertrand Russell concerned himself with mysticism and was, according to himself, influenced by a “mathematical mysticism” in his younger years.

In his essay “Mysticism and Logic” (Russell 1918) Russell understands mysticism as “the attempt to conceive the world as a whole by means of thought”. He gives four characteristics of it:

“belief in insight as against discursive knowledge”
a belief in unity of everything
denial of the reality of time
the claim that evil, and sometimes also good, is a mere appearance
Russell finds at least some of these characteristics in the philosophies of Heraclitus, Plato, Hegel, and Spinoza. Interestingly, Heraclitus is judged far better than Plato, the former being ascribed “a nature [in which] we see the true union of the mystic and the man of science”. In the remainder of the essay Russell discusses the relation of the four characteristics of mysticism to his own views.

In the autobiographical book Portraits from Memory the passage

Mathematics … deals with the world of ideas and has in consequence an exactness and perfection which is absent from the everyday world. This kind of mathematical mysticism, which Plato derived from Pythagoras, appealed to me.

may serve as an example how Russell was influenced in young age by the exposure to mathematics; more poetically it is expressed in the essay The Study of Mathematics published along with Mysticism and Logic (Russell 1918)

Mathematics, rightly viewed, possesses not only truth, but supreme beauty—a beauty cold and austere, like that of sculpture, without the gorgeous trappings of painting or music, yet sublimely pure, and capable of a stern perfection such as only the greatest art can show. The true spirit of delight, the exaltation, the sense of being more than man, which is the touchstone of the highest excellence, is to be found in mathematics as surely as in poetry. … Real life is, to most men, a long second-best, a perpetual compromise between the ideal and the possible; but the world of pure reason knows no compromise, no practical limitations, no barrier to the creative activity embodying in splendid edifices the passionate aspiration after the perfect from which all great works springs.

… Of the austere virtues the love of truth is the chief, and in mathematics, more than elsewhere, the love of truth may find encouragement for waning faith.

According to Ray Monk’s biography on Russell, the search for a foundation of this “Pythagorean” mysticism governed the first half of his life: Being deeply disappointed by the mathematical curriculum at Cambridge, which did not address his philosophical needs, Russell turned to idealism, which was at that time propounded in Britain by J.M. Ellis McTaggart following the German tradition of Kant and Hegel. Under this influence Russell devised in An Essay on the Foundations of Geometry a variation of Kant’s transcendental aesthetics claiming that the curvature of the space of our perception, i.e. of any ‘’form of externality’’, is a priori constant.

Exposure to the work of the German mathematicians Dedekind, Weierstraß, and Cantor along with a personal meeting with Peano caused a turn in Russell’s views. He now hoped to find a rigorous foundation of mathematics based solely on logical axioms, thereby justifying a kind of Platonic view on mathematics. But over the years he was frustrated in this attempt by many problems he encountered, especially Russell's paradox. He gradually gave up all his Platonic beliefs; arriving in the end (after Wittgenstein's Tractatus) at formalism.

He remarks on the power of rigorous mathematical definition:

“Continuity” had been, until he [Cantor] defined it, a vague word, convenient for philosophers like Hegel, who wished to introduce metaphysical muddles into mathematics. Cantor gave a precise significance to the word, and showed that continuity, as he defined it, was the concept needed by mathematicians and physicist. By this means a great deal of mysticism, such as that of Bergson, was rendered antiquated. (Chapter XXXI of “A History of Western Philosophy” (1945))

3. Brouwer
L.E.J. Brouwer had a long standing interest in the theory and practice of mysticism, setting out his manifesto while still a graduate student in the essay Life, Art, and Mysticism (1905). The essay quotes the Bhagavad Gita, Meister Eckhart, and Jakob Böhme.

However, he did not consider his intuitionism to depend upon his mystical views as such. For Brouwer, mysticism is the domain of “consciousness’ deepest home”, wherein there is no subject-object distinction. The first act of intuitionism, the intuition of time, propels us away from this pure state of “wisdom”. It is in fact the precondition for any experience of an outer world or experience of the self as something distinct. Mathematics thus comes into being in this exodus from the home of consciousness, so on Brouwer’s view, “mathematics is in a sense the very opposite of mysticism” (Van Atten, 2004), and mystical insight is only possible quite apart from the machinations of the intellect.

Brouwer even went so far as to remark on the perniciousness of mathematics in its keeping us from the home of consciousness. Thus in the notebooks in which he conceived his 1907 thesis we find: “One could see as the goal of one’s life: abolition and delivery from all mathematics”.

4. Gödel
For the moment, see e.g. van Atten and Tragesser 2014, and Gödel’s ontological proof involving modal logic.

  blob 2a79fe25018cce7e99a2c33786d88b0551db6ae7, byline Nathan McKnight,
  document date June 2025: repeats the 1D-curve / 4D-volume wording.

The direct Kerr-section statement does not specify the section's intrinsic
dimension, the sweep parameter's relation to the SAT-O1 affine parameter,
the actual sweep map, its differential, its image, or any quotient/fiber
structure. The SAT-O1 curve and the later Kerr-section proposal are separate
source objects; no map identifying them is supplied.

## Formal scope

SweepLinearization stores a candidate linear map from the product of a
section tangent space and a one-dimensional filament-parameter tangent
space into a four-dimensional ambient tangent space. It does not prove that
the supplied linear map is the derivative of an existing smooth sweep map.

The theorems use Mathlib's finite-dimensional rank-nullity theorem:

- If the section is 3D and the candidate differential is injective, its
  image rank is 4. This is the full-dimensional branch, compatible with a
  4D-volume interpretation.
- If the section is 3D but the intended local image rank is 3, the kernel
  must have dimension 1. A quotient/fiber-collapse or other rank-defect
  construction is therefore an additional obligation.
- If the section is 2D and the differential is injective, the image rank is
  3. This is a different dimensional branch, not an assertion about which
  section Nathan intended.

The rank statements are local linear algebra only. They do not establish
smoothness, constant rank, an embedded submanifold, a global quotient,
Kerr geometry, a metric, a timesheet map, or a physical worldtube.
-/

namespace HsHVerification.RavelKerrSectionSweepRankGate

variable {K : Type*} [Field K]
variable {SectionTangent FilamentParameterTangent AmbientTangent : Type*}
  [AddCommGroup SectionTangent] [Module K SectionTangent]
  [FiniteDimensional K SectionTangent]
  [AddCommGroup FilamentParameterTangent] [Module K FilamentParameterTangent]
  [FiniteDimensional K FilamentParameterTangent]
  [AddCommGroup AmbientTangent] [Module K AmbientTangent]
  [FiniteDimensional K AmbientTangent]

/-- A supplied first-order candidate for extending a spatial section along
    a one-dimensional filament parameter into four-dimensional spacetime.
    The source-to-map correspondence and smooth-map derivative are not
    supplied by this structure. -/
structure SweepLinearization where
  sectionDimension : Nat
  sectionDimension_eq :
    Module.finrank K SectionTangent = sectionDimension
  filamentParameterDimension_eq :
    Module.finrank K FilamentParameterTangent = 1
  ambientDimension_eq :
    Module.finrank K AmbientTangent = 4
  differential :
    (SectionTangent × FilamentParameterTangent) →ₗ[K] AmbientTangent

namespace SweepLinearization

variable (S : SweepLinearization (K := K)
  (SectionTangent := SectionTangent)
  (FilamentParameterTangent := FilamentParameterTangent)
  (AmbientTangent := AmbientTangent))

/-- The actual rank-nullity identity for the supplied linearized sweep map. -/
theorem rank_add_nullity :
    Module.finrank K (LinearMap.range S.differential) +
      Module.finrank K (LinearMap.ker S.differential) =
      Module.finrank K (SectionTangent × FilamentParameterTangent) :=
  S.differential.finrank_range_add_finrank_ker

/-- The product tangent-space dimension is section dimension plus one
    filament-parameter dimension. -/
theorem domain_dimension :
    Module.finrank K (SectionTangent × FilamentParameterTangent) =
      S.sectionDimension + 1 := by
  rw [Module.finrank_prod, S.sectionDimension_eq,
    S.filamentParameterDimension_eq]

/-- A 3D section swept along one parameter has a 4D domain. If its
    differential is injective, the local linearized image has rank four. -/
theorem three_dimensional_section_injective_rank_four
    (hSection : S.sectionDimension = 3)
    (hInjective : Function.Injective S.differential) :
    Module.finrank K (LinearMap.range S.differential) = 4 := by
  have hKer : LinearMap.ker S.differential = ⊥ :=
    LinearMap.ker_eq_bot.mpr hInjective
  have hNull : Module.finrank K (LinearMap.ker S.differential) = 0 := by
    rw [hKer]
    simp
  have hDomain : Module.finrank K
      (SectionTangent × FilamentParameterTangent) = 4 := by
    rw [S.domain_dimension, hSection]
  have hRankNullity := S.rank_add_nullity
  rw [hDomain, hNull] at hRankNullity
  omega

/-- If a 3D section sweep is intended to have a 3D local image, its
    four-dimensional domain differential must have a one-dimensional kernel. -/
theorem three_dimensional_section_rank_three_requires_one_kernel_dimension
    (hSection : S.sectionDimension = 3)
    (hRank : Module.finrank K (LinearMap.range S.differential) = 3) :
    Module.finrank K (LinearMap.ker S.differential) = 1 := by
  have hDomain : Module.finrank K
      (SectionTangent × FilamentParameterTangent) = 4 := by
    rw [S.domain_dimension, hSection]
  have hRankNullity := S.rank_add_nullity
  rw [hDomain, hRank] at hRankNullity
  omega

/-- A rank-three image from a 3D section sweep is incompatible with an
    injective differential. -/
theorem three_dimensional_section_rank_three_not_injective
    (hSection : S.sectionDimension = 3)
    (hRank : Module.finrank K (LinearMap.range S.differential) = 3) :
    ¬ Function.Injective S.differential := by
  intro hInjective
  have hFull :=
    S.three_dimensional_section_injective_rank_four hSection hInjective
  omega

/-- A 2D section swept along one parameter has a 3D domain. If its
    differential is injective, the local linearized image has rank three. -/
theorem two_dimensional_section_injective_rank_three
    (hSection : S.sectionDimension = 2)
    (hInjective : Function.Injective S.differential) :
    Module.finrank K (LinearMap.range S.differential) = 3 := by
  have hKer : LinearMap.ker S.differential = ⊥ :=
    LinearMap.ker_eq_bot.mpr hInjective
  have hNull : Module.finrank K (LinearMap.ker S.differential) = 0 := by
    rw [hKer]
    simp
  have hDomain : Module.finrank K
      (SectionTangent × FilamentParameterTangent) = 3 := by
    rw [S.domain_dimension, hSection]
  have hRankNullity := S.rank_add_nullity
  rw [hDomain, hNull] at hRankNullity
  omega

/-- In the 3D-section/injective branch, the linearized image has the same
    dimension as the four-dimensional ambient tangent space. -/
theorem three_dimensional_full_rank_fills_ambient_dimension
    (hSection : S.sectionDimension = 3)
    (hInjective : Function.Injective S.differential) :
    Module.finrank K (LinearMap.range S.differential) =
      Module.finrank K AmbientTangent := by
  calc
    Module.finrank K (LinearMap.range S.differential) = 4 :=
      S.three_dimensional_section_injective_rank_four hSection hInjective
    _ = Module.finrank K AmbientTangent := S.ambientDimension_eq.symm

end SweepLinearization

#print axioms SweepLinearization.rank_add_nullity
#print axioms SweepLinearization.domain_dimension
#print axioms SweepLinearization.three_dimensional_section_injective_rank_four
#print axioms SweepLinearization.three_dimensional_section_rank_three_requires_one_kernel_dimension
#print axioms SweepLinearization.three_dimensional_section_rank_three_not_injective
#print axioms SweepLinearization.two_dimensional_section_injective_rank_three
#print axioms SweepLinearization.three_dimensional_full_rank_fills_ambient_dimension

end HsHVerification.RavelKerrSectionSweepRankGate
",
